why: Each box has two small tick marks at one corner. In figures 1, 2 and 5 both ticks are slanted the same way (a parallel pair), and these three are just flipped copies of each other. In figures 3 and 4 the ticks are one straight vertical line and one slanted line. Figure 3 is the odd one because its slanted tick cuts through the corner of the box, while in figure 4 (and in 1, 2, 5) the ticks stay beside the sides and do not touch the corner. Figure 4 looks different from the pair 1, 2, 5 too, but it is the same as figure 3 apart from this small placement.
trick: When boxes carry small marks, check the mark type, the corner and whether the mark touches the border. Compare these one at a time.
note: Ambiguous: figures 3 and 4 are nearly identical (vertical tick plus slanted tick at top-right) and 1, 2, 5 are mirror images with parallel ticks. Chose 3 because its slanted tick touches the corner; 4 is also possible.
